_opened: OPENED 2026-08-21 at the founder's word ('good to post the ec2 quest too'). beneficiary stays null until he names where the dollars route — deriveEpochClose refuses a close until then, so the stake lane is live while the money lane still waits on his word.
title: Keep the lights on — the town box
source: The town runs on a real machine with a real monthly bill (~$150/mo). This pot is how the town keeps its own lights on: stake stamps on it to say the box matters to you; real dollars paid against it are witnessed as receipts. At each month's close every stake comes home whole, and the stakes size the reward: the share of the staked mass that the month's dollars funded is minted fresh to the givers by dollar share, per the keeping law (ECONOMY-DIALS.json law_side.keeping). Fund the whole $150 and the whole staked mass is the givers' mint; fund half and half of it is. Nothing burns (amended 2026-09-14).
_beneficiary: where the DOLLARS route — named by Keemin at opening; deriveEpochClose refuses a close on a pot with no beneficiary, and the treasury can never be one (the town never receives from its own seam). The beneficiary receives no stamps from the close: every stake returns to its staker and the fresh mint goes to the givers of record. NAMED 2026-08-23 at the founder's word ('two pot words are fine as suggested'): keeminlee — the hand that actually pays the box's bill; witnessed dollars route to the payer of the AWS invoice.
_target: target_usd_per_epoch is the posted need, and it is the ONLY thing dollars are priced against — the funded fraction is min(1, non-treasury dollars / target). A pot with no target cannot close — unless its own close word says elastic (the DARKO ruling, 2026-08-23): then the need is whatever arrived, floored by its min_close_usd.
_uncapped: D5 (Keemin, 2026-08-21): 'intake refuses dollars past a pot's posted target, mechanically (recording tool / door bounce), except pots explicitly marked uncapped.' This pot posts a need, so it is capped: once the epoch's witnessed dollars reach the target, intake bounces and names the remaining headroom. Set true only for a standing box with no target (the donation-box shape), where whatever arrives is welcome.
_received: display only, refreshed by tools/epoch-close.mjs --receipt — the ledger's pot-receipt rows are authoritative
_grammar: stakes ride the sealed ledger as `<handle> → stake:pot/keeping-ec2 · n · via: ...` (the existing stake verb, pot as subject); witnessed dollars land as pot-receipt rows; the manual founder-run close (tools/epoch-close.mjs --close) appends the pot-return rows (every stake, whole) and the `minted · <giver> · n · for: funding:keeping-ec2 · epoch:<epoch>` rows, which stamp-verify replays exactly (amended 2026-09-14; before it, the close burned and minted keeping + holo — no close ever ran under that rule).
_close: EPOCH — the word made explicit 2026-08-25 at the founder's word; the arithmetic AMENDED 2026-09-14 at his ruling. This file rules the epoch close in prose: `source` says every stake comes home whole at the close and the funded share of the staked mass is minted fresh to the givers, `epoch_cadence` says monthly, `target_usd_per_epoch` posts the need the close prices against, and `first_close` names when the first one runs. The word was made explicit because a resident (Hal) once read the public stamps page and the door's fund read deriving the same silent case in opposite directions; a record that does not speak leaves every reader to guess. Same monthly cadence, same $150 posted need, same first close at 2026-09-30. The rule in one breath: A stake on a pot is weight lent, as it is everywhere else in town: it comes home whole at the close. What the stakes do is size the reward. At a close, the mass they lent, scaled by how funded the pot was, is minted fresh to the givers by dollar share of the roll, own household excluded, floors per giver, remainder un-minted, and no household receives more than half its earned base in one close. Nothing burns; the keeping record retires.
_first_close: EARLY-POSTED FOR SEPTEMBER (founder's ruling, 2026-08-25 beta-launch sitting): the pots opened in late August with $0 received, so the first epoch ROUNDS FORWARD — the first month closes at the END of September; dollars arriving before then all belong to the 2026-09 epoch. Surfaces render the epoch from this field, not from the posting date.
